legal_basis: ICA_S124_01 (Indian Contract Act ss.124-125, indemnity) was considered because the clause is substantively an indemnity, but its trigger_condition ('indemnity obligation is uncapped or unusually broad in scope') is NOT met -- see notes. No rule is asserted.
annotation_notes: CATEGORY MISMATCH -- PRIMARY FINDING. This span is assigned 'Dispute Resolution' via CUAD 'Covenant Not To Sue', but its text is a release / defend / indemnify / hold-harmless clause. It contains no forum-selection, arbitration, or bar-on-proceedings language. The assigned category does not describe the clause. Held at Moderate rather than High because two genuine limits are present in the text: the indemnity is confined to Claims arising from Customer's OWN breach of its representations/warranties/covenants, and it is proportionately carved back for Transporter's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Those are meaningful protections, not symbolic ones. AMBIGUITY 0.25: unusually precise for its type -- 'Claims' is expressly defined inline and the carve-out is explicit. Residual 0.25 for 'proportionate extent', which requires apportionment machinery not visible here. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00: no applicable rule; ICA_S124_01 trigger not met. ENFORCEABILITY 0.25: low residual only. The gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct carve-out is precisely the feature whose ABSENCE would raise concern.
ai_uncertainty_note: Because the clause's true subject (indemnity) is not its assigned category (Dispute Resolution), the rule inventory was searched by substance rather than by category label. A human should confirm that this is the right way to resolve a category/substance conflict -- the guidelines do not currently say.

Should NOT be scored as risk-increasing merely because it shares a category with Non-Compete -- requires a separate polarity flag before any risk scoring is built on top of it.

Here the restriction IS bounded on three axes: a numeric cap (no more than two other agreements), a temporal limit ('During the Term'), and express carve-outs. Trigger not met; no rule asserted.
annotation_notes: POLARITY CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY. Phase 1 flagged CUAD 'Competitive Restriction Exception' as a risk-REDUCING carve-out wrongly grouped with risk-increasing Non-Compete. This clause shows the flag was right but incomplete: the span is BOTH at once. Its first half imposes a restriction (CNET may not enter more than two competing-retailer promotion agreements); its second half carves out standard advertisements, COMPUTERS.COM and Snap!. A single polarity label could not describe this span. UNFAIRNESS 0.25: binds CNET only, so it is one-directional -- but it is a negotiated in-term commercial cap with substantial express exclusions, not a blanket prohibition. AMBIGUITY 0.50: 'standard advertisements', 'fixed promotions' and 'permanent links' are undefined and carry real weight, since they mark the boundary between prohibited and permitted conduct. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00: ICA_S27_01 trigger not met (see legal_basis). ENFORCEABILITY 0.25: residual only. Note this is an IN-TERM restriction on contracting with third parties, not a post-termination restraint on CNET's own trade; the rule's own exception_condition treats that distinction as context-dependent, and it is not resolved here.
ai_uncertainty_note: Whether an in-term exclusivity-style cap engages s.27 at all is context-dependent and the inventory does not settle it. Confidence Low.
ai_guideline_issue: A span can simultaneously restrict AND carve out. Neither the guidelines nor the schema provide a way to record mixed polarity within one record.

clause_text: Both Parties agree that during the Term of this Agreement and for a period of two (2) years following the termination, both Parties will not (i) solicit, encourage, or take any other action, which is intended, directly or indirectly, to induce any employee to terminate his or her employment with a Party; or (ii) interfere in any manner with the contractual or employment relationship between the Parties and any their employees.
mapping_reason: Direct match.
legal_basis: ICA_S27_02 (rule_type=risk_trigger) applied. Its trigger_condition is that the restriction is 'broad/indefinite in scope or duration'. Duration here is definite (two years) and does NOT meet the trigger, but scope does: limb (ii) prohibits interference 'in any manner' with any employment relationship, which is open-ended in a way limb (i) is not. Applied on the scope limb only. Consistent with the rule's exception_condition, this is flagged as a matter for review rather than treated as a conclusion -- Indian courts assess reasonableness on the facts, and post-termination employee non-solicitation is treated differently from a restraint on a party's own trade.
annotation_notes: The only clause in the pilot where a rule's trigger_condition is affirmatively met, and the only Medium provisional level. UNFAIRNESS 0.25: expressly mutual ('Both Parties ... both Parties'), so the burden is symmetric -- this is why unfairness stays Low despite the restriction being substantive. AMBIGUITY 0.50: 'interfere in any manner' is vague and load-bearing; 'take any other action, which is intended, directly or indirectly, to induce' is broad; and the text contains an apparent drafting error ('between the Parties and any their employees'). NON_COMPLIANCE 0.25: partial trigger only -- scope limb met, duration limb not. Deliberately not higher, because a two-year, mutual, employee-focused non-solicit is not the paradigm s.27 case. ENFORCEABILITY 0.50: the breadth of limb (ii) is a genuine and reviewable concern, stated as a concern rather than a conclusion.
ai_uncertainty_note: The gap between limb (i) (narrow, conventional) and limb (ii) (broad) is the whole question. A human may reasonably score non_compliance 0.00 by reading the clause as a single conventional non-solicit, or 0.50 by weighting limb (ii) more heavily. This is the clause most likely to produce genuine inter-annotator disagreement.
ai_guideline_issue: No instruction exists for partial trigger satisfaction -- where a rule's trigger_condition has two limbs and only one is met.

On the visible text the payment trigger is Dova's own termination under Section 12.3.1, and the payment is consideration for promotion services already performed during the Term -- not a stipulated consequence of a breach by Valeant. Applying s.74 here would be exactly the 'liquidated damages = illegal penalty' error the methodology warns against. No rule asserted.

CUAD labels this 'Liquidated Damages' and the mapping sends it to 'Penalties', but the text reads as a post-termination tail-compensation provision protecting the SERVICE PROVIDER (Valeant) for work performed, payable when the CLIENT (Dova) terminates. It is compensatory in direction, not punitive. UNFAIRNESS 0.25: the clause favours Valeant, and the party bearing the obligation (Dova) is the one who triggers it by its own election to terminate. Low. AMBIGUITY 0.50: the multiplier is redacted '[***]', and 'Tail Period', Section 12.3.1 and Section 6.1 are all outside the span. NON_COMPLIANCE 0.00: ICA_S74_01 trigger not met (see legal_basis).
